gloss: an unexpected guest; someone who arrives uninvited
teaser: Have you ever had a surprise visitor that turned your day upside down?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Have you ever had a surprise visitor that turned your day upside down?[break 1s]The phrase is: 不速之客, bù sù zhī kè.[break 0.5s]不 (bù) means 'not'[break 0.5s]速 (sù) means 'speed' or 'fast'[break 0.5s]之 (zhī) is a possessive particle, similar to 'of'[break 0.5s]客 (kè) means 'guest' or 'visitor'[break 1s]So, the full idiom 不速之客 literally means 'an uninvited guest.' Figuratively, it refers to someone who arrives unexpectedly.[break 1s]Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s]In ancient China, it was common for hosts to prepare extensively for guests. A visitor who arrived unannounced could disrupt the host's plans and cause chaos. Over time, this phrase began to symbolize not just unexpected guests but any surprise that can throw off one's routine.[break 1.5s]Example one: 他是一个不速之客。  He is an unexpected guest.[break 1s]Example two: 这种不速之客真让人感到惊讶。 This kind of unexpected guest really surprises people.[break 1s]Example three: 我们准备了很多食物，但他是个不速之客。 We prepared a lot of food, but he was an uninvited guest.[break 1s]So, 不速之客 means 'an unexpected guest.'
